cut_items.item: Error responses (500, proxy/gateway failures) often lack CORS headers, so the browser shows the CORS message and hides the real error; check the status code in the Network tab
A redirect (e.g. HTTP to HTTPS) can drop the CORS headers; call the final URL
CORS middleware must be registered before the routes
The browser sends an Origin header and the server must reply with Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to that origin (mechanism explanation)
Asks for the Network tab request headers to help diagnose

added_items.item: Setting CORS headers in both a proxy and the app produces duplicate values that the browser rejects; set them in one place

Raw header example (Allow-Origin, Allow-Methods, Allow-Headers) for any stack

Run CORS before auth middleware so 401/500 responses include the headers
Restart the API and reload the frontend after changing it
If you cannot change the API, use a dev proxy (dev only)
